youtube.aciklama: Auditory nerve fibers tend to fire at the same phase of the sound wave; this is called phase locking. Because a single fiber can fire at most a few hundred times per second, Wever's volley principle says different fibers fire on different cycles and, as a group, mark every cycle.

cumleler: Can a single nerve fiber follow a thousand-hertz sound?
Fibers fire at the same wave phase; this is phase locking.
A single fiber fires at most a few hundred times per second.
Alone, that is not enough to follow a thousand-hertz wave.
In the volley principle, fibers take turns; the group marks every cycle.
In mammals, clear phase locking fades above about four to five kilohertz.
